name: Markus Saueregger
sources: “‘verschiedenARTig’: Brigitte Bock präsentiert neue Werke in Kötschach-Mauthen”, gailtal-journal.at, 12 February 2026
“Markus Saueregger: ‘Ich bin gerne in der Natur unterwegs’”, meinbezirk.at, 28 February 2018
text_en: Markus Saueregger comes from Afritz in the Gegendtal and has lived with his family in Dellach im Gailtal for about 20 years; by profession he works in nursing care. Before he opened the stARTup gallery, he showed two exhibitions at other places in Kötschach-Mauthen, the Biachakastl and the Café Zuckereck. In May 2023 he opened the gallery rooms at Kötschach 5. Since then he has shown artists from the Gail valley and Upper Carinthia there, among them Hannes Grimmer, Herta Hofer, Walther Preiml, Heidulf Gerngross, Claudia Unterluggauer and Brigitte Bock. In 2024 he led a one-day “Kunstmeile” in Kötschach: 17 artists showed works in shops and cafés of the village and in the Protestant church. The idea for the day came from local small businesses that the closure of the nearby Plöcken Pass hit hard.

name: Barbara Ambrusch-Rapp
text_en: Barbara Ambrusch-Rapp was born in 1972 in Klagenfurt and works as a freelance multimedia artist, cultural worker and curator in Velden am Wörthersee. She takes part in exhibitions, performance, theatre, fashion art and projects in public space, and gives creative workshops. She chairs the art association postWERK and received the Kultur-Ehrenzeichen of the City of Villach in 2026.

name: Walter Hösel
text_en: Walter Hösel initiated and organises the annual design experiments of ARS CARINTHIA – KUNST & HANDWERK in Klagenfurt, in which artists and architects develop objects together with Carinthian craft businesses. In 2026 the tenth experiment, „INSIEME“, marked 30 years of KUNST & HANDWERK with exhibitions at several venues in Klagenfurt; he curated its exhibition „DIALOG“ at the Stadtgalerie Klagenfurt. He also makes his own objects, such as the series „CALIBOC“ (2026), developed with Elisabeth Raunig and several craft businesses.

name: Manfred Ortner
text_en: Manfred Ortner was born in Linz in 1943 and studied painting and art education at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna from 1961 to 1967. After working as an art teacher, he joined the group Haus-Rucker-Co in Düsseldorf in 1971, where he worked with Günter Zamp Kelp and his brother Laurids Ortner until 1987, the year the brothers founded Ortner & Ortner Baukunst (today O&O Baukunst). From 1994 to 2012 he was professor of design at the architecture faculty of FH Potsdam; in 2020 he and his brother received the Grand Austrian State Prize.

name: Marlies Rapetti
text_en: Marlies Liekfeld-Rapetti was born in 1939 in Königsberg, East Prussia, and grew up in the GDR and West Germany. She trained as a medical technical assistant, studied art and German studies, and worked in teaching, in museum education and with a private painting school. She lived in Carinthia from 1985 to 2009 and in Berlin from 2009 to 2015, and has lived and worked in Klagenfurt since 2016; she works with paper and textiles and makes installations.

name: Andreas Kuchler
sources: “Wie aus Krieg Frieden wird”, klick-kaernten.at, 7 May 2025
“Mittendrin: Die Museumsstandorte Villachs als urbane Identitätslabore”, museumsbund.at, 2 June 2025
text_en: Andreas Kuchler is the director of the Museum der Stadt Villach. He presented its special exhibition “Wie Kriege enden / How wars end” in 2025 and led curator’s tours through it. In 2025 he wrote about the museum’s sites in Villach for the Museumsbund Österreich.

name: Christl Wiegele
text_en: Christl Wiegele was born in 1937 in Töbring near Treffen and died in September 2020. She lived in Radendorf. Her father was the Villach painter LUWALL (Ludwig Wallner). From 1995 she took lessons with Sigi Braun, Heribert Mader, Inge Peischl, Bernhard Vogel and Wolfgang Wiesinger. She joined postWERK in 2014 and had solo exhibitions in Afritz, Albeck, Finkenstein, Arnoldstein and Villach.

name: Ulli Sturm
text_en: Ulli Sturm is an art educator and curator in Klagenfurt. In 2020 she and the artist Jochen Traar set up the „kunstbureau“ at Waagplatz 5 in Klagenfurt, a room for talks, readings and small site-specific exhibitions. For the Stadtgalerie Klagenfurt she curated „NO PLANET B“ at the Alpen-Adria-Galerie (2025–2026) and „ALL ABOUT NATURE – Zwischen Idylle, Krise und Hoffnung“ at the Stadtgalerie (2026).

name: Karsten Krebs
text_en: Karsten K. Krebs was born in Zeulenroda in 1945 and studied architecture and urban planning in Hanover and Florence. He runs the office Karsten K. Krebs Architekten in Hanover and has taught as professor of spatial art (Raumkunst) at the Peter Behrens School of Arts in Düsseldorf. His work covers architecture, interior and garden design, product design, light and art, and he has taken part in several of the art and craft projects of ARS CARINTHIA in Klagenfurt.

name: Elisabeth Juan
text_en: Elisabeth Juan is the secretary on the board of BV Kärnten, the Carinthian branch of the Berufsvereinigung der bildenden Künstler Österreichs, which runs the BV Galerie in Klagenfurt. The association also lists her among its members.

name: Siegfried Zellot
text_en: Siegfried Zellot, who signs his work as Zesi, was born on 29 August 1953 in Spittal an der Drau. From 2012 to 2016 he studied at the Freie Akademie der bildenden Künste Kärnten, continued in Luka Anticevic’s master class from 2016 and took courses in etching and screen printing at the Freie Kunst Akademie Augsburg. He works in acrylic and oil, drawing, objects and printmaking, and teaches acrylic painting and print techniques at the Kunstverein Velden. He lives and works in Mallenitzen am Faaker See.

name: Edith Payer
text_en: Edith Payer was born in Wolfsberg, Carinthia, in 1975 and studied visual arts at the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna from 1998 to 2003, with a period at the Kuvataideakatemia in Helsinki in 2001. Her work is based on collecting found objects and images, which she arranges into museum-like installations and groups of objects. She also realises participatory exhibition projects together with other artists, makes textile works, often from used materials, and draws artist's books. She lives and works in Vienna and in Redlschlag.

name: Jörg Auzinger
text_en: Jörg Auzinger was born in 1972 in Linz. After training in audiovisual media and photography at the Ortweinschule in Graz with Richard Kriesche, he studied media art with Peter Weibel at the University of Applied Arts Vienna and film directing with Axel Corti at the Vienna Film Academy. In interactive installations, photographs and objects he examines how digital media affect perception and communication. He has taught media art and photography at the Ortweinschule Graz and was a visiting professor at the University of Applied Arts Vienna; he lives and works in Vienna and Styria.

name: Markus Guschelbauer
text_en: Markus Guschelbauer was born on 24 December 1974 in Friesach, Carinthia. From 2003 to 2009 he studied photography at the Institute of Fine Arts and Media Art of the University of Applied Arts Vienna, and he has worked as a freelance artist since his diploma in 2009. His work deals with landscape: he stages interventions in nature with everyday materials such as plastic sheeting, fabric, mirrors and wooden slats and records them with the camera. He lives and works in Vienna.

name: Herbert Meißlitzer
sources: “Alpen-Adria-Kunst im Stadthaus: Trigeniale 24 – Kunst aus dem Herzen Europas”, meinbezirk.at, 18 October 2024
text_en: Herbert Meißlitzer from Klagenfurt has been painting since 1991, working in watercolour, acrylic, acrylic collage and oil. He is a member of the International Watercolor Society Austria. His acrylic paintings show landscapes and well-known townscapes. In 2017 he showed his work for the sixth time in an exhibition in his family's garden in Klagenfurt-Viktring.

name: Anita Wiegele
text_en: Anita Wiegele was born in 1964 in Villach and works as a freelance artist, author and performer in Gödersdorf. She graduated from the Freie Akademie der Bildenden Künste and Literatur-Kärnten and illustrates book projects. She published the books “Kopfverklebung – ein Prozess” (2016) and “Wolkenköpfe” (2017). She received the Kultur-Ehrenzeichen of the City of Villach in 2021.

name: Aleksandra Rusjan
sources: “Kunst in den Hügeln: Trigeniale Brda im Herbst”, meinbezirk.at, 28 September 2026
text_en: Aleksandra Rusjan is a painter from Goriška Brda in Slovenia and a member of the artists’ association DABLO (Društvo briških likovnih ustvarjalcev) in Brda. In autumn 2026 she exhibited with Giulia Cernetig and Margrit Pernull in Trigeniale Brda 26 at the Kmetija Moro in Vipolže. Her works there included “Kanjon” (canyon), “Češnja” (cherry), which she called her favourite work, and a painting of Dobrovo Castle.

name: Lilith Erian
text_en: Lilith Erian is a visual artist who works mainly with photography, including landscape, portrait and travel photography. In 2024 the Kulturhof Villach showed her series “Aushalten – Zdržati”, portraits of ten young people from the cultural scene of Carinthia/Koroška combined with their own statements. In 2025, at the age of 22, she was the youngest artist so far to show in the series “Kunst am roten Teppich” at the SPÖ parliamentary club in Klagenfurt.

name: Aus der Asche empor – Skulptur und Stickerei
sources: invitation of the Galerie im Schloss Porcia
text_en: Announcement. This exhibition has not opened yet. Under the title “Aus der Asche empor” (rising from the ashes), Sylvia Ofner shows sculpture and embroidery in the Salamancakeller of Schloss Porcia. From old oriental carpets, heirlooms and needlework of the 1930s she sews mythological figures: phoenix and centaur, Europa and the bull, Gilgamesh, Lamassu and the sphinx. With needle and thread she spins a story from the roots of Europe in Egypt and Mesopotamia to the present, a Europe that has reinvented itself again and again after wars and crises. The setting echoes the theme: the palace was built in the Renaissance, the age that saw itself as the rebirth of antiquity.

name: Gernot Fischer-Kondratovitch – vintage views from an unknown future
sources: “Ab 12. November: Vintage in der Galerie Freihausgasse”, villach.at, 4 November 2026
text_en: Announcement. This exhibition has not opened yet. The Galerie Freihausgasse shows paintings by Gernot Fischer-Kondratovitch, born in Villach in 1968, under the title “vintage views from an unknown future”. According to the gallery they show pictures from a distant future: people, containers, houses and exotic animals in landscapes of ice and snow, or palm trees, beaches and seas in front of mountains. One of the works is from the series “Schneehaluzinationen” of 2026, acrylic on canvas, 100 × 140 cm.

name: Mediterraneo – Ölbilder von Harald Scheicher
sources: “Die Werkschau zeigt über 2300 Ölbilder des Malers Harald Scheicher.”, scheicher.cc
text_en: For the ORF Lange Nacht der Museen on 3 October 2026, the Galerie Palais Fugger in Klagenfurt showed oil paintings by the Carinthian painter Harald Scheicher under the title “Mediterraneo”. A grandson of Werner Berg, Scheicher has painted outdoors in front of the motif for decades; besides the landscape of southern Carinthia, painting journeys regularly take him to Istria, Dalmatia and Sicily. From 18:00 the artist guided visitors through the exhibition and was available for conversation; children could join tours, puzzle rallies and drawing. Whether the exhibition stayed on view after that night is not documented.

name: Wagner reloaded
text_en: Since 2011 the Stadttheater Klagenfurt has staged Richard Wagner with marked intensity, from Der fliegende Holländer to Tristan und Isolde. The Theatergalerie shows four costumes from Wagner’s Walküre and Tristan und Isolde together with their designs, and turns to the work behind the curtain: the theatre’s tailoring and make-up departments, headed by Bettina Breitenecker and Renate Wutte. Stage photographs by Arnold Pöschl accompany the costumes. Curated by Günter Schmidauer, in cooperation with the Stadttheater Klagenfurt, which lent the works. The room also holds Burgis Paier’s permanent installation Das große Welttheater.

name: Volkskino Klagenfurt
text_en: The Volkskino at Kinoplatz 3 in Klagenfurt shows current films, film classics, silent films and original-language versions, and offers screenings for schools. The federal funding list for programme cinemas for 2026 names it as “Alternativkino Klagenfurt, Neues Volkskino”. In 2026 the cinema marks 100 years of the Volkskino.

name: Lebenshilfe Region Knittelfeld
sources: “Willkommen im ‘Ideenreich’ – unserem inklusiven Verkaufslokal mit integrierter Produktionsstätte”, ideenreich-knittelfeld.at
“Knittelfeld: Das ‘Ideenreich’ eröffnete mit Pauken und Trompeten”, meinbezirk.at, 20 March 2025
text_en: The Lebenshilfe Region Knittelfeld began on 3 February 1982 as a parents’ association and today is a non-profit company with its association behind it, chaired by Johann Hubmann. Nearly 100 people work in its workshops, homes and mobile services for people with intellectual disabilities. It is a member of the Lebenshilfe network in Austria. In the shop “Ideenreich” at Hauptplatz 17 it sells products made in its workshops.
